spec.problem: The app saves which chat is open but throws that away when it loads. `serialize` (src/lib/chat/store.ts:150-152) writes the whole `ChatState`, including `activeId`. Selecting a chat in the sidebar changes `activeId` through the `select` action (store.ts:87-90), and the persist effect in src/App.tsx:167-178 saves that change. On reload, App.tsx:61 calls `deserialize`, which ignores the saved `data.activeId` and always sets `activeId = chats[0]?.id ?? null` (store.ts:164). That is the most recently updated chat, not the one the user was reading. So after a reload the app opens the newest chat instead of the selected one.

The existing test (`activeId: "bad"` gives "c1") already covers the dropped-chat case and must still pass.

Add the unit tests in chat.test.ts after line 133.
Run `pnpm check-types && pnpm lint && pnpm test`. Then check in `pnpm dev`: select an older chat, reload, and the same chat is open.

spec.problem: The message timestamp label counts 24-hour periods since the message, not calendar days. `src/lib/chat/time.ts:10` computes `days = Math.floor((now - at) / DAY)`. A message sent at 11:50 PM and read at 12:10 AM is 20 minutes old, so `days` is 0 and the label is "Today 11:50 PM" (lines 16-21). A message from late evening two days ago, read the next morning, is under 48 hours old, so `days` is 1 and the label is "Yesterday". The same off-by-one moves the boundaries for the weekday label (line 23, `days < 7`) and for the full date. The existing tests in `src/lib/chat/time.test.ts` miss it because each fixture is far enough from the 8:13 PM `NOW` that elapsed days and calendar days agree.

files.why: Count calendar days in the viewer's local time zone. Take the difference between local midnight of `now` and local midnight of `at` (for example `new Date(y, m, d).getTime()` for each) and round it with `Math.round(... / DAY)` so that a DST day of 23 or 25 hours still counts as one day. Today, Yesterday, the weekday label and the full date then all switch at midnight.

tests.why: Add cases that cross midnight. 11:50 PM yesterday seen at 12:10 AM must give "Yesterday 11:50 PM". 11:00 PM two days ago seen the next morning must give the weekday name, not "Yesterday". A message 6 calendar days ago but under 6x24h old must still give the weekday, and one 7 calendar days ago must give the full date. Add a case across a DST change, for example the last Sunday of October in Europe, which only fails when the test run uses a time zone with DST.

plan: In messageTime, replace the elapsed-time day count with a calendar-day difference between the local midnights of `now` and `at`, rounded to absorb DST hours.
Keep the existing thresholds (<2 relative word, <7 weekday, otherwise date). Keep the clamp `Math.max(0, days)` for timestamps slightly in the future.
Add the midnight-crossing tests that build `NOW` with `new Date(...)` in local time, then run pnpm check-types && pnpm lint && pnpm test.
assumptions: "Today" and "Yesterday" should follow the viewer's local calendar day. The browser's local time zone is the right reference; there is no per-user time zone setting.
The weekday window ("within the last week") should also count in calendar days, so a message from 7 calendar days ago shows the date and not a weekday name that is ambiguous with today's.
Labels are computed when a message is rendered. If an open chat does not re-render at midnight, labels stay stale until the next render. That is a separate concern and is not part of this fix.

spec.problem:
The privacy panel files hosts with `classifyHost` in `src/lib/privacy/network.ts:20-24`, using the patterns in `MODEL_HOSTS` at `src/lib/privacy/network.ts:18`. The first pattern, `/(^|\.)huggingface\.co$/`, is anchored to a label boundary. The second, `/hf\.co$/`, is not, so it matches any host that ends in the letters "hf.co". That includes `evilhf.co`, `nothf.co` and `attacker-hf.co`. All of these are classed as "model" and shown under "Model files (download only, nothing is uploaded)". This misleads the panel whose job is to show what leaves the device.

spec.problem: If you click another chat in the sidebar while an answer is still streaming, the answer is lost. The cause is in the reducer. The `token` and `finish` cases in `src/lib/chat/store.ts:118-137` don't write to the chat the action names. They write to `state.activeId ?? action.chatId`. `send()` in `src/App.tsx:240-260` sets `chatId` correctly to the chat being written (it also records it in `writingChat`). But once the user selects another chat (`select` sets `activeId`, store.ts:87-90), every later token batch goes to the newly active chat. The assistant message id doesn't exist in that chat, so `mapMessage` matches nothing and the text is silently dropped. The original chat keeps the empty placeholder that `send` created (store.ts:115), and `finish` stats are lost the same way. Nothing throws, so there is no error, which matches the report. The `fail` case (store.ts:139) already uses `action.chatId`, so failures land in the right chat. Saving to storage is skipped while `generating` is true (App.tsx:172) and resumes after `finish`, so once the reducer is fixed the full answer is saved.

Add a reducer test where the active chat changes mid-stream and the tokens still land in the original chat.
Run `pnpm check-types && pnpm lint && pnpm test`.
Check by hand in a browser (`pnpm dev`, WebGPU): start a long answer, switch to an older chat, switch back, and confirm the answer is complete and still there after a reload.

spec.problem:
The cross-tab sync merges chats the wrong way. When tab 1 saves, tab 2's `storage` listener (`src/App.tsx:143-164`) dispatches `{ type: "sync" }`. The reducer's `sync` case (`src/lib/chat/store.ts:100-106`) builds a union of the incoming chats and this tab's chats, and this tab's copy wins on every id clash (line 103: `for (const c of state.chats) byId.set(c.id, c)`). That causes both symptoms in the issue:
1. Deleted chats come back. Chats deleted in tab 1 are missing from `incoming`, but tab 2 still has them in `state.chats`, so they survive the merge. The persist effect skips this one state change (`fromOtherTab`, `src/App.tsx:168-171`). The next local change in tab 2 (select, send, new) writes the whole stale list back to localStorage. Tab 1 then merges it back in too.
2. New messages don't show up. If tab 2 already had the chat, its older copy overwrites tab 1's newer one, so tab 2 never shows the new messages, and its next save also removes them from storage.
Only "delete everything" works, because it takes the separate `clear` path (`src/App.tsx:148-153`). The existing tests (`src/lib/chat/chat.test.ts:155-181`) only cover adding chats and keeping the chat being streamed into, so the bug went unnoticed.

files.why: Change the sync semantics: the incoming state is authoritative for which chats exist and what they contain. The only exception is `keepChatId`, the chat this tab is still streaming into: keep the local version and put it into the list. Fall back to the first chat for `activeId` when the open chat was deleted elsewhere. Update the comments on the action type and in the reducer to match.

tests.why: Inside `describe("sync from another tab")`, add cases: (a) a chat missing from `incoming` is removed locally; (b) when a chat exists in both, the incoming copy with more messages replaces the local one; (c) if the active chat was deleted in the other tab, `activeId` falls back to the first remaining chat, or null if none are left; (d) a `keepChatId` chat missing from `incoming` is still kept with its local content, if that is the decided behaviour. Keep the existing two cases passing.

plan: In `chatReducer`'s `sync` case, start from `action.incoming.chats`. If `keepChatId` is set and that chat exists locally, put the local version in place of the incoming one, or add it if the incoming list doesn't have it. Sort by `updatedAt` descending, as now.
Keep `state.activeId` if that chat is still in the result. Otherwise use `chats[0]?.id ?? null`.
Update the comments at `store.ts:32` and `store.ts:101`. Check that the comment at `App.tsx:141-142` is still accurate; no logic change is expected in App.tsx.
Add the reducer tests listed above to `chat.test.ts`.

Run `pnpm check-types && pnpm lint && pnpm test`. Then check by hand in two tabs of `pnpm preview`: delete a chat in tab 1, act in tab 2, and confirm it stays deleted; send in tab 1 to a chat that is open in tab 2, and confirm the message appears in tab 2.
assumptions: Last writer wins across tabs is acceptable. Every local change except streamed tokens is saved straight away (`App.tsx:167-178`), so localStorage always holds the newest committed state, and the incoming value can replace the local one without losing work.
The only unsaved local state is the answer being streamed (saving is paused while `generating`). That chat is identified by `writingChat`/`keepChatId`, so protecting it alone is enough.
There's a smaller race this fix doesn't cover: if both tabs stream at the same time, the second save overwrites the first tab's answer. That is out of scope for this issue.
open_questions: If the other tab deletes the chat this tab is still streaming into, should this tab keep the chat (it reappears in the other tab when the answer is saved) or drop it and interrupt the engine, as the wipe-all path already does? The spec assumes keeping it, to match the current `keepChatId` contract.

spec.problem: Each new message reaches the model with only the last stored message of the conversation. That last message is the assistant's previous reply, so every earlier user message is lost. `send()` in src/App.tsx:249-253 builds the prompt as [system, ...toModelMessages(history).slice(-HISTORY_TURNS), new user message], and `HISTORY_TURNS = 1` (src/App.tsx:52). `toModelMessages` (src/lib/chat/store.ts:193-199) returns one entry per message, not per turn, so `slice(-1)` keeps a single message. In the issue's example, the model gets [system, assistant "Nice to meet you...", user "what's my name?"] and never sees the message with the name. This doesn't depend on the model, which matches the report that two models behave the same. The rest of the pipeline already supports full history. The comment at src/App.tsx:51 says "the worker trims further to fit the context window". `fitToContext` in src/lib/engine/worker.ts:161-179 drops the oldest turns once the prompt is over MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS (4096). docs/REVIEW-GUIDE.md:67-68 says "History is re-sent in full each turn". So the cap of 1 is the bug, either a leftover debugging value or the confusion between turns and messages.

spec.problem: Model output is rendered with react-markdown in `src/components/message.tsx:55`. The custom `markdownComponents` (`src/components/message.tsx:12-19`) only override `a`. Nothing overrides `img`, so a reply like `![x](https://host/a.png)` becomes a real `` and the browser fetches it. That is a request to a third-party host, triggered by model output and possibly carrying data in the URL. In production the CSP `img-src 'self' data: blob:` (`vite.config.ts:19`) blocks it. `pnpm dev` has no CSP (`vite.config.ts:33`, CLAUDE.md), so the request goes out, which matches the report. `docs/REVIEW-GUIDE.md:52-53` says "Images are replaced by their alt text in code", but the code does not do this, so code and docs disagree. The code should never create the request in any build. It should not rely on the production CSP. Side finding, not the cause: the comment at `message.tsx:12` says links open in a new tab, but the `a` override sets no `target="_blank"`.
